name: High-protein one-pot ptitim rosé 'risotto' (ריזוטו פתיתים רוזה)

source.author: Pasted recipe (Hebrew)
source.notes: Everything in one wide pot: 500 g ptitim (Israeli couscous), 1 kg cottage cheese 5% (4 tubs), 150 g 9% yellow cheese, olive oil, a 350 g jar of tomato sauce, garlic, paprika, salt, pepper and chili flakes, cooked with 2–3 cups water until creamy; finished with grated parmesan. Analyzed as 8 servings (~270 g each). Tomato sauce taken as a standard jarred pasta sauce; parmesan ~5 g per serving. Manual intake — kept as reference, not adopted. Estimate.

ingredients.note: whole-wheat/spelt ptitim adds fibre if available

ingredients.item: yellow cheese 9%, grated or thinly sliced

ingredients.note: the cottage, cheese and jarred sauce are already salty — see mods

ingredients.qty: 2 cups to start, up to 1 more as needed

steps: Put the ptitim in a wide pot; add the cottage, yellow cheese, olive oil, tomato sauce and garlic.
Add the paprika, salt, pepper and chili flakes, pour in 2 cups water and stir gently so the liquid reaches the bottom.
Cover and bring to a boil on high, stirring gently now and then.
Lower to medium-low and cook covered ~8–10 min.
Uncover, stir and check — add ¼ cup water at a time if needed; cook uncovered ~4–5 min more, stirring, until the ptitim is tender and the sauce coats it.
Turn off, cover 2 min to settle, and serve with grated parmesan. It thickens as it cools and turns creamy again when reheated.

batch_totals.note: Whole pot (8 servings). The 1 kg of cottage is what makes it 'protein-packed' — it supplies about half the protein. Sodium is the standout issue: cottage, yellow cheese, the jarred sauce and parmesan are all salty before the 1½ tsp of added salt goes in.

him.verdict: A genuinely clever comfort-food bowl: the kilo of cottage melted into the sauce gives ~28 g protein per serving in what eats like a creamy pasta, with tomato sauce adding lycopene (a sperm-priority micro). It's still pasta-led (~54 g carbs, ~6.3 g protein per 100 kcal), and sodium is high at ~1,170 mg per serving — almost all of the added salt is unnecessary on top of four salty dairy/sauce ingredients.
flags: ~28 g protein per serving — cottage does the heavy lifting
pasta-led: ~54 g carbs, ~6.3 g protein per 100 kcal
high sodium (~1,170 mg) — cottage + yellow cheese + jarred sauce + parmesan + 1½ tsp salt
one pot, reheats well — good meal-prep
suggested_mods: Cut the added salt to a pinch (or none) and taste at the end — this alone drops sodium by ~430 mg/serving
Use whole-wheat or spelt ptitim for fibre
Use 400 g ptitim instead of 500 g and keep all the cottage — protein density goes up
Stir in spinach or peas at the end for fibre, folate and volume
Use a low-sugar / low-sodium tomato sauce

her_preconception.verdict: Good calcium and protein from all that cottage, fully cooked, all pasteurized cheeses — no safety flags. But it's high in sodium and offers little folate or iron as written. Folding in a couple of handfuls of spinach and cutting the salt would make it a solid regular for her.
suggested_mods: Fold in spinach at the end for folate + iron

cooking_guide: Use a WIDE pot so the ptitim cooks in an even layer — in a narrow, deep pot the bottom scorches before the top is done.
After adding the water, stir gently right down to the base so the liquid reaches the bottom; cottage-based sauces stick and catch easily.
Stir gently every couple of minutes, especially once it's boiling — scraping the bottom is what prevents burning.
Add extra water only ¼ cup at a time; ptitim absorbs quickly, and it's easy to overshoot into soup.
Hold off on salt until the end and taste — the cheeses and the jarred sauce may already be enough.
Take it off the heat slightly looser than you want; it thickens a lot while resting. Reheat with a splash of water to bring back the creaminess.
